title: 03. Agents from Scratch: Layer 3: Agent Architectures 1/3: What Is This Layer About? · The Big Picture — Why Architecture Matters …
summary: Agent Architecture = How you ORGANIZE agents to solve problems. > Just like a company has org charts — CEO → Managers → Workers — AI agents also need structure.
objectives: The Big Picture — Why Architecture Matters

sections.title: What Is This Layer About?
sections.body:
> **Agent Architecture = How you ORGANIZE agents to solve problems.**
> Just like a company has org charts — CEO → Managers → Workers — AI agents also need structure. The architecture you choose determines how fast, accurate, and cost-effective your system is.

sections.title: The Big Picture — Why Architecture Matters
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              WHY AGENT ARCHITECTURE MATTERS                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  TASK: "Research Python best practices, write a blog post,
          add code examples, review it, and publish it"

  BAD APPROACH — ONE AGENT DOES EVERYTHING:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  [Single Agent]
       ↓
  Tries to do all 5 things sequentially
  Gets confused switching between roles
  Quality suffers — jack of all trades, master of none
  If it fails at step 3, you restart from scratch
  Takes forever — cannot parallelize

  GOOD APPROACH — RIGHT ARCHITECTURE:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  [Supervisor]
      ├── [Researcher Agent]  → finds best practices
      ├── [Writer Agent]      → writes blog post
      ├── [Coder Agent]       → adds code examples
      ├── [Reviewer Agent]    → checks quality
      └── [Publisher Agent]   → formats and publishes

  Each agent is SPECIALIZED → Better quality
  Agents can run in PARALLEL → Faster
  One agent fails? → Only retry that agent
  Easy to SWAP one agent → Modular

  ARCHITECTURE IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN:
  ┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Wrong Architecture      │  Right Architecture              │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
  │  Slow (sequential)       │  Fast (parallel)                 │
  │  Low quality (confused)  │  High quality (specialized)      │
  │  Hard to debug           │  Easy to debug (isolated)        │
  │  Fragile (one fail=all)  │  Resilient (isolated failures)   │
  │  Expensive (wasteful)    │  Cost-efficient (right model)    │
  └──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: All Architecture Patterns — Overview
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           8 AGENT ARCHITECTURE PATTERNS                         │
├────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────── │
│ #  │  Pattern             │  One-line description               │
├────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────── │
│ 1  │  Single Agent        │  One agent + tools, ReAct loop      │
│ 2  │  Supervisor          │  Boss agent delegates to workers     │
│ 3  │  Router              │  Dispatcher sends to right agent     │
│ 4  │  Pipeline (Chain)    │  Output of one feeds next            │
│ 5  │  Reflection          │  Agent critiques its own output      │
│ 6  │  Parallel (Fan-out)  │  Multiple agents work simultaneously │
│ 7  │  Debate              │  Agents argue, judge picks best      │
│ 8  │  Hierarchical        │  Multi-level tree of agents          │
└────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────── │
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body:
> One agent. One loop. Reason → Act → Observe → Repeat until done.
> This is the **foundation** of all agents. Every other architecture is built on top of this.

sections.title: When to Use Single Agent
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             SINGLE AGENT — WHEN TO USE IT                       │
│                                                                 │
│  ✅ USE WHEN:                                                   │
│  • Task needs 1–5 tool calls                                    │
│  • Task can be done by ONE type of expert                       │
│  • Simplicity matters more than scale                           │
│  • You're prototyping / learning                                │
│                                                                 │
│  ❌ AVOID WHEN:                                                 │
│  • Task needs 10+ steps (use Supervisor)                        │
│  • Task needs multiple domains of expertise                     │
│  • Parts can run in parallel (use Parallel pattern)             │
│  • Quality is critical (use Reflection)                         │
│                                                                 │
│  REAL EXAMPLES:                                                 │
│  ✅ "Search for X and summarize it"      → Single Agent         │
│  ✅ "Calculate compound interest"        → Single Agent         │
│  ✅ "Translate this text to Spanish"     → Single Agent         │
│  ❌ "Research, write, review, publish"  → Supervisor            │
│  ❌ "Analyze 5 stocks simultaneously"   → Parallel              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > A **Supervisor (boss) agent** receives the task, **breaks it into subtasks**, **delegates** each subtask to the right **worker agent**, **collects results**, and **synthesizes** the final answer.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               SUPERVISOR PATTERN — FULL FLOW                    │
│                                                                 │
│  TASK: "Build a Python FastAPI app for user authentication"     │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                    SUPERVISOR AGENT                     │   │
│  │  Receives task → Plans → Delegates → Synthesizes        │   │
│  │                                                         │   │
│  │  Plan created:                                          │   │
│  │  1. Research → "find FastAPI auth best practices"       │   │
│  │  2. Code     → "write the auth endpoints"               │   │
│  │  3. Test     → "write test cases"                       │   │
│  │  4. Document → "write README"                           │   │
│  └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘   │
│          ┌──────────────┼──────────────┬──────────────┐        │
│          ▼              ▼              ▼              ▼         │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌───────┐ │
│  │  RESEARCHER  │ │   CODER      │ │   TESTER     │ │WRITER │ │
│  │    AGENT     │ │   AGENT      │ │   AGENT      │ │ AGENT │ │
│  │              │ │              │ │              │ │       │ │
│  │ Finds:       │ │ Writes:      │ │ Writes:      │ │Writes:│ │
│  │ • JWT auth   │ │ • /register  │ │ • test_login │ │README │ │
│  │ • bcrypt     │ │ • /login     │ │ • test_reg   │ │ docs  │ │
│  │ • OAuth2     │ │ • /refresh   │ │ • test_token │ │       │ │
│  └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └───┬───┘ │
│         │                │                │              │     │
│         └────────────────┴────────────────┴──────────────┘     │
│                                   │                             │
│                                   ▼                             │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                 SUPERVISOR SYNTHESIZES                  │   │
│  │  Takes all 4 results → combines into complete project   │   │
│  │  Checks consistency → fills gaps → final output         │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                 │
│  KEY POINTS:                                                    │
│  • Supervisor has BROAD knowledge (knows what to delegate)     │
│  • Workers have DEEP knowledge (experts in their domain)       │
│  • Supervisor can run workers SEQUENTIALLY or IN PARALLEL      │
│  • Supervisor can RETRY failed workers                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > A **Router** is a smart dispatcher. It reads the incoming query, **classifies it**, and **routes it** to the most suitable specialized agent. The router itself doesn't answer — it just directs traffic.

sections.title: How Routing Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  ROUTER PATTERN — FULL FLOW                     │
│                                                                 │
│  INCOMING QUERIES:                                              │
│  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────     │
│  "What is 2345 * 6789?"         → Math query                   │
│  "Write a bubble sort"          → Code query                    │
│  "What is the A2A protocol?"    → Research query                │
│  "Translate to Spanish"         → Language query                │
│  "Analyze this CSV data"        → Data query                    │
│                                                                 │
│                    │                                            │
│                    ▼                                            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                    ROUTER AGENT                         │   │
│  │                                                         │   │
│  │  1. Read query                                          │   │
│  │  2. Classify: {route: "math", confidence: 0.97}         │   │
│  │  3. Select correct agent                                │   │
│  │  4. Forward query + context to that agent               │   │
│  └──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                     │                                           │
│        ┌────────────┼────────────┬───────────┬──────────┐      │
│        ▼            ▼            ▼           ▼          ▼      │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐  │
│  │  MATH    │ │  CODE    │ │RESEARCH │ │  LANG  │ │  DATA  │  │
│  │  AGENT   │ │  AGENT   │ │  AGENT  │ │  AGENT │ │  AGENT │  │
│  │          │ │          │ │         │ │        │ │        │  │
│  │ Uses:    │ │ Uses:    │ │ Uses:   │ │ Uses:  │ │ Uses:  │  │
│  │calculator│ │ executor │ │  search │ │  trans │ │ pandas │  │
│  │  solver  │ │  linter  │ │   wiki  │ │  -late │ │  stats │  │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └─────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  WHY ROUTER IS POWERFUL:                                        │
│  • Each specialized agent has DEEP expertise                    │
│  • No agent is confused by off-topic requests                   │
│  • Easy to ADD new specialized agents                           │
│  • Easy to UPGRADE individual agents independently              │
│  • Can use DIFFERENT models (GPT-4o for code, mini for math)    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Router vs Supervisor
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              ROUTER vs SUPERVISOR — KEY DIFFERENCES             │
│                                                                 │
│  ROUTER:                                                        │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  • ONE agent handles the FULL task                              │
│  • Router just PICKS which agent                                │
│  • No combining/synthesis needed                                │
│  • "This is a math question → Math Agent → Done"               │
│                                                                 │
│  Query → Router → ONE Agent → Answer                           │
│                                                                 │
│  SUPERVISOR:                                                    │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  • Task is SPLIT into multiple subtasks                         │
│  • MULTIPLE workers each do a part                              │
│  • Supervisor COMBINES all results                              │
│  • "This needs research + code + docs"                          │
│                                                                 │
│  Task → Supervisor → Multiple Workers → Synthesis → Answer     │
│                                                                 │
│  USE ROUTER WHEN:          USE SUPERVISOR WHEN:                 │
│  ─────────────────         ────────────────────                 │
│  • Query has clear type    • Task has multiple parts            │
│  • One expert is enough    • Need multiple experts              │
│  • Fast response needed    • Quality > speed                    │
│  • Simple classification   • Complex orchestration              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Agents arranged in a **sequence**. Agent 1's output becomes Agent 2's input. Like an assembly line — each station adds value before passing to the next.

sections.title: How Pipeline Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               PIPELINE PATTERN — FULL FLOW                      │
│                                                                 │
│  TASK: "Research AI trends, write a report, translate to        │
│          French, format as PDF"                                 │
│                                                                 │
│  RAW QUERY                                                      │
│       │                                                         │
│       ▼                                                         │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐                         │
│  │  STAGE 1: RESEARCHER               │                         │
│  │  Input:  "Research AI trends"      │                         │
│  │  Output: 5 key findings about      │                         │
│  │          current AI trends         │                         │
│  └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘                         │
│                     │  (passes findings)                        │
│                     ▼                                           │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐                         │
│  │  STAGE 2: WRITER                   │                         │
│  │  Input:  5 findings from Stage 1   │                         │
│  │  Output: 500-word structured report│                         │
│  └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘                         │
│                     │  (passes report)                          │
│                     ▼                                           │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐                         │
│  │  STAGE 3: TRANSLATOR               │                         │
│  │  Input:  English report            │                         │
│  │  Output: French report             │                         │
│  └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘                         │
│                     │  (passes French text)                     │
│                     ▼                                           │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐                         │
│  │  STAGE 4: FORMATTER                │                         │
│  │  Input:  French report             │                         │
│  │  Output: PDF-ready formatted doc   │                         │
│  └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘                         │
│                     │                                           │
│                     ▼                                           │
│             FINAL OUTPUT ✅                                      │
│                                                                 │
│  PIPELINE RULES:                                                │
│  ✅ Each stage gets the FULL output of the previous stage       │
│  ✅ Each stage can also get the ORIGINAL query for context      │
│  ✅ Stages are INDEPENDENT — easy to swap/upgrade               │
│  ⚠️  Slow — stages run SEQUENTIALLY (cannot parallelize)        │
│  ⚠️  Error in stage 2 = stages 3&4 also fail                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > An agent **generates** an output, then a **critic** reviews it, then the generator **improves** based on feedback. This loop continues until quality is acceptable. Like having a peer reviewer for your work.

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Multiple agents work **at the same time** (concurrently) on **different parts** of the same task. Results are collected and **merged**. This is the fastest pattern.

sections.title: How Parallel Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              PARALLEL PATTERN — FAN-OUT / FAN-IN                │
│                                                                 │
│  TASK: "Analyze these 5 stocks: AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN, META" │
│                                                                 │
│  SEQUENTIAL (slow):                                             │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  AAPL→[Agent]→done  GOOGL→[Agent]→done  MSFT→...               │
│  ├─── 3 sec ───┤├─── 3 sec ───┤├─── 3 sec ───┤...             │
│  Total: 5 × 3s = 15 seconds ❌ SLOW                             │
│                                                                 │
│  PARALLEL (fast):                                               │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  FAN-OUT → All agents start simultaneously                       │
│                                                                 │
│  AAPL  ──→ [Agent 1] ──┐                                        │
│  GOOGL ──→ [Agent 2] ──┤                                        │
│  MSFT  ──→ [Agent 3] ──┼──→ [AGGREGATOR] ──→ Combined Report   │
│  AMZN  ──→ [Agent 4] ──┤                                        │
│  META  ──→ [Agent 5] ──┘                                        │
│                                                                 │
│  All run at same time → finish in 3 seconds ✅ 5x FASTER!       │
│                                                                 │
│  FAN-OUT PHASE: Distribute work to N agents simultaneously      │
│  FAN-IN PHASE:  Collect all results and merge them             │
│                                                                 │
│  AGGREGATOR does:                                               │
│  • Waits for ALL agents to complete (or timeout)                │
│  • Collects all results                                         │
│  • Merges/synthesizes into final output                         │
│  • Handles failures (some agents may fail)                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Multiple agents **argue** for their best answer, then a **judge** picks the winner. Like a courtroom — multiple perspectives → best truth emerges.

sections.title: How Debate Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               DEBATE PATTERN — FULL FLOW                        │
│                                                                 │
│  QUESTION: "Is Python or Go better for building AI agents?"     │
│                                                                 │
│  ROUND 1 — OPENING ARGUMENTS:                                   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Agent A (Python advocate):                              │  │
│  │  "Python wins: massive AI ecosystem (PyTorch, LangChain) │  │
│  │   fast prototyping, Jupyter notebooks, huge community"   │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Agent B (Go advocate):                                  │  │
│  │  "Go wins: 10x faster execution, native concurrency,     │  │
│  │   single binary deployment, better for production scale" │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  ROUND 2 — REBUTTALS:                                           │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Agent A rebuttal:                                       │  │
│  │  "Go lacks mature LLM SDKs. Python has async/await now.  │  │
│  │   Go's ecosystem for AI is immature compared to Python"  │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Agent B rebuttal:                                       │  │
│  │  "Python's GIL limits true parallelism. In production,   │  │
│  │   latency matters. Go handles 100K concurrent requests." │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  JUDGE evaluates:                                               │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Criteria: Evidence quality, logic, completeness         │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  │  Verdict: "DEPENDS ON USE CASE.                          │  │
│  │  Python → research, prototyping, ML-heavy workloads      │  │
│  │  Go     → production microservices, high throughput      │  │
│  │  Both agents made valid points. Context matters most."   │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  WHY DEBATE IS POWERFUL:                                        │
│  • Forces agents to find WEAKNESSES in each other's answers    │
│  • Produces more nuanced, balanced final answer                │
│  • Great for controversial or complex questions                 │
│  • Judge catches logical errors that generators miss           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > A **tree of agents** with multiple levels. Top-level agents delegate to mid-level managers, who delegate to specialized workers. Used for **very complex, large-scale tasks**.

sections.title: How Hierarchical Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            HIERARCHICAL PATTERN — FULL STRUCTURE                │
│                                                                 │
│  TASK: "Build a complete e-commerce website"                    │
│                                                                 │
│                    ┌────────────────┐                           │
│                    │  CEO AGENT     │                           │
│                    │  (Top Level)   │                           │
│                    │  Plans overall │                           │
│                    │  strategy      │                           │
│                    └───────┬────────┘                           │
│           ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐                   │
│           ▼                ▼                ▼                   │
│  ┌────────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐           │
│  │ FRONTEND MGR   │ │ BACKEND MGR │ │  DEVOPS MGR  │           │
│  │  (Mid Level)   │ │ (Mid Level) │ │  (Mid Level) │           │
│  └───────┬────────┘ └──────┬──────┘ └──────┬───────┘           │
│     ┌────┴────┐       ┌────┴────┐      ┌────┴────┐             │
│     ▼         ▼       ▼         ▼      ▼         ▼             │
│ ┌───────┐ ┌───────┐ ┌───────┐ ┌────┐ ┌────┐ ┌───────┐         │
│ │  UI   │ │  UX   │ │  API  │ │ DB │ │ CI │ │Monitor│         │
│ │ Agent │ │ Agent │ │ Agent │ │Agt │ │/CD │ │ Agent │         │
│ └───────┘ └───────┘ └───────┘ └────┘ └────┘ └───────┘         │
│                                                                 │
│  INFORMATION FLOWS:                                             │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  DOWN: CEO → Managers → Workers                                 │
│  Tasks, requirements, constraints flow downward                 │
│                                                                 │
│  UP: Workers → Managers → CEO                                   │
│  Results, status, problems flow upward                          │
│                                                                 │
│  WHEN TO USE HIERARCHICAL:                                      │
│  ✅ Very large, complex tasks (build entire app)                │
│  ✅ Multiple domains of expertise needed                        │
│  ✅ Need coordination between departments                       │
│  ❌ Overkill for simple tasks → use Supervisor instead          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

A Router is a smart dispatcher. It reads the incoming query, classifies it, and routes it to the most suitable specialized agent.
quiz.explanation: A Router is a smart dispatcher. It reads the incoming query, classifies it, and routes it to the most suitable specialized agent. The router itself doesn't answer — it just directs traffic.
